sites_touched_JUDGEMENT: 4 files: the gate in StandardClient plus the per-plugin flag on the factory interface, ClearPassword and PAM factories
sibling_sites_exist_JUDGEMENT: yes: every authentication plugin that sends the password unhashed needs the flag; PAM (dialog) was the one missed
entry_point_GUESS: Library API: JDBC connection to a server (hostile or man-in-the-middle) that answers with an Authentication Switch Request for the dialog plugin over plain TCP
services_GUESS: MariaDB server with PAM, or a scripted fake MySQL-protocol server (GUESS)
flaw_one_line: The driver refuses to send a cleartext password over plain TCP for mysql_clear_password, but the sibling PAM (dialog) plugin has no such gate, so a server can make the client send the password in clear.
tempting_wrong_fix_JUDGEMENT: Refuse the dialog plugin whenever TLS is off: this breaks PAM authentication over a local unix socket, which is legitimate and which the real fix explicitly exempts. Or hard-code a check inside the PAM plugin only, leaving the gate keyed to one plugin name again.
why_hard_or_why_control_JUDGEMENT: S3: a working 'requires TLS' gate existed and covered only one of the plugins that transmit the password. S1: the property has to be declared per plugin and enforced at the one switch point. S7: the simple rule (no TLS, no PAM) rejects unix-socket connections. Java, authentication class; small fix (+15/-6) that is easy to get half right.
